generic_sampling_rules.int_primary_key: Sequential integers starting at 1; never NULL; unique per table; PK columns are excluded from DISTINCT/GROUP/ORDER shaping so uniqueness is preserved.
generic_sampling_rules.int_foreign_key: Copy an existing parent primary-key value from the parent keys actually inserted in this instance; 10% of rows get NULL when the column is nullable; ensure at least one parent row has no child and at least one child row has NULL FK; re-verify after PK dedup.
generic_sampling_rules.int_numeric: Uniform integer in [1, 100] unless a per-column exception gives a tighter range; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.real_numeric: Uniform real in [1990.0, 2010.0] with one decimal; never NULL when NOT NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Pick from a small pool of 8-12 distinct plausible strings; 20-40% duplicate share; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Pick from a pool of 10-15 distinct person/place names; 20-40% duplicate share; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: Pick uniformly from the enum values listed in per_column_exceptions; 20-40% duplicate share; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_like_variant: For LIKE/equality literals, include the exact literal, a lowercase variant, an uppercase variant, and one near-variant (e.g. 'glish' for 'English'); 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_boundary: For comparison literals, include the exact literal and one lexicographic step on each side; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_wl_record: Format 'W-L' with W,L integers 0-9; 20-40% duplicate share; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_years: Format 'N (YYYY-YYYY, ...)' with N 1-10; 20-40% duplicate share; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: Every nullable column gets at least one NULL row per instance; share 5-10%; planted NULLs are preserved through semantic rules (three-valued logic).
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_duplicates: Every DISTINCT-target non-PK column gets 20-50% duplicate share.
generic_sampling_rules.order_ties: Every ORDER-target column gets at least two rows tied at the first rank.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: Every GROUP-target non-PK column gets groups of size 1, 2 and >=3.

issues.title: Generated instances lose compact rows (compact_rows_missing = 20/20) despite writer claiming to copy them
issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports validity.reasons.compact_rows_missing = 20 and new_integrity_failures = 20, with fk_violations = 411. writer.write_instance_sqlite only copies the compact DB when orig_path is not None (either passed as argument or read from getattr(schema, 'orig_path', None)). In cli._one, write_instance_sqlite(_G['schema'], inst, p) is called without orig_path, and read_schema never sets schema.orig_path (the Schema dataclass has no such field and read_schema does not assign it). Therefore the compact DB is never copied: writer falls back to executing schema.ddl and inserting only generated rows into a fresh DB. That directly contradicts the module docstring ('Every instance is a *copy of the compact database plus appended generated rows*') and the specification's preservation intent.
issues.requested_revision: Wire orig_path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. set schema.orig_path = orig_path in read_schema, or pass the original DB path into _one and call write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, orig_path)). Re-run and confirm compact_rows_missing == 0 and that new_integrity_failures/fk_violations drop accordingly.

issues.title: Guaranteed FK NULL and parent-without-child guarantees broken by PK dedup and by cross-instance independent parent generation
issues.evidence: Integrity shows fk_violations = 411 across 20 instances. fill_foreign_keys_consistently plants values from _parent_values (compact rows only, since generated parent rows are inserted after child sampling because the schema.table_order puts children implicitly before parents for match_season.Country/Team in some topological levels — the topological order places match_season before player/team in table_order levels; actually table_order is computed from tdeps and match_season depends on team and country, so team/country should come first, but original_values for parent columns of team/country may be sparse). More concretely: after fill_foreign_keys_consistently plants NULLs, sample_fresh_primary_keys then drops whole rows whose PK tuple repeats, which can remove either the only NULL-FK child row or the only 'parent without children' alignment; and the resulting values can be fine, but the parent side relies on compact rows that are not present (see first issue), so children can reference parent PKs that never get inserted, causing FK violations. Also the spec required 'at least one parent row has no child and at least one child row has NULL FK' is not enforced structurally, only hoped for.
issues.requested_revision: Order tables so parents are committed before children (already intended via topological table_order — verify with the actual schema.table_order emitted for this DB), and revalidate after PK dedup that each nullable FK still retains ≥1 NULL row and that at least one parent PK in each referenced parent table has no referencing child. When building match_season.Country/Team and player.Team, draw FK values only from parent PKs that will actually be inserted in the same instance (intersect _parent_values with the final generated parent keys plus compact keys), and assert after dedup.

issues.title: No rows added for several instances (no_rows_added = 15/20)
issues.evidence: validity.reasons.no_rows_added = 15 out of 20. rows_added shows 50/131/315/175 aggregated, but per-instance many instances added 0 rows in some/all tables. choose_table_sizes uses round(base * (0.5 + rng.random())) which for small bases (e.g. 6, 10, 16) can yield 0 (uniform over [0.5, 1.5) → round can give 0 for base ≤ ~1, but even base 6 rounds to 3..9; however sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates can reduce to 0 when _shape_groups/duplicates collapse the PK column of generated rows to duplicates relative to the compact PKs (sample_fresh_primary_keys keeps first occurrence only per PK tuple, and Team_id/Country_id are in DISTINCT_TARGETS — _shape_duplicates can overwrite many PKs with copies of earlier values, so the PK dedup collapses the table to 1 row typically, and potentially 0 if there are edge cases). Combined with drop_unique_duplicates on unique columns this can zero out tables.
issues.requested_revision: Do not apply DISTINCT/duplicate/tie shaping to primary-key columns (exclude PK columns from DISTINCT_TARGETS and ORDER_TARGETS/GROUP_TARGETS shaping), or apply shaping before generating PKs with fresh guaranteed-unique sequential integers per the specification ('Sequential integers starting at 1; never NULL; unique per table'). The specification's int_primary_key rule requires sequential unique PKs; the current DISTINCT shaping on country.Country_id and team.Team_id violates that rule. Also verify generated_rows_per_instance ≥ 1 per table is preserved after dedup.

issues.title: Specification inconsistency: int_primary_key rule says sequential unique PKs but per_column_exceptions and duplicates_for_distinct require 20-50% duplicate share on PK columns
issues.evidence: Generation specification 'int_primary_key' says 'Sequential integers starting at 1; never NULL; unique per table.' Yet per_column_exceptions include {"table":"country","column":"Country_id","pattern":"duplicates_for_distinct","targets":"20-50% duplicate share"} and the same for team.Team_id, plus group_sizes {'country.Country_id'} requiring groups of size 1, 2 and ≥3 (impossible for a unique sequential PK). The extracted atomic operations also include duplicates_for_distinct and group_sizes patterns on PK columns. These are logically contradictory.
issues.requested_revision: Resolve the contradiction: either state that the DISTINCT/GROUP/duplicate-share patterns are applied to *sample values before PK assignment* (with the PK reassigned uniquely), or remove the duplicate/group targets from PK columns in the specification. The program should follow whichever resolution is chosen; the current program implements the duplicate-share variant, then falls back to PK dedup, which silently defeats the pattern and causes no_rows_added/compact_rows_missing effects.

issues.title: Unsupported rules not asserted from data
issues.evidence: Several semantic rules are stated without enough evidence to be safe as generation constraints; e.g. 'match_season.Position IN (Defender, Midfielder, Forward)' is claimed but the comparison_boundary targets explicitly include 'defender','midfielder','forward' (lowercase) for Position, and BOUNDARY[(match_season, Position)] includes those, contradicting the IN-domain. Similarly, 'match_season.Player' and 'match_season.Draft_Class' are constrained to the literal set ['Duke','duke'] by the boundary targets, which is implausible as a real domain (Duke is a college, not a player/draft class) — this comes from the extraction of a cross-column predicate PRED(college='UCLA' OR player='Duke') being misinterpreted as a per-column boundary constraint. These are recorded in the spec without evidence.
issues.requested_revision: Revise supporting evidence for Position (the boundary targets must be uppercase only, aligned with the IN-domain, or the IN-domain must be widened to include case variants), and remove the Player/Draft_Class boundary pools of ['Duke','duke'] — these are artifacts of a cross-column OR predicate and should not constrain a single column's domain.

issues.title: Nullable columns sometimes get 0 NULL rows after shaping
issues.evidence: nullable_columns shows several columns with NULL 0/n: match_season.College (0/18), match_season.Draft_Pick_Number (0/18). The specification's null_share rule and per-instance rule require every nullable column to get at least one NULL row per instance. _apply_null_rule runs before _apply_semantic_rules, and _apply_semantic_rules for College/Draft_Pick_Number (via BOUNDARY / INT_RANGES) overwrites NULLs with sampled values (for Position it uses 'v if v is None else …' which preserves NULLs, but for Draft_Pick_Number it uses 'v if v is None or v > 0 else …' preserving NULLs — however Draft_Pick_Number's NULL comes from _apply_null_rule but there is also a redundant (t, cm.name)-keyed branch; more critically, College 0/18 means the sampler before _apply_null_rule produced values that were then reshaped, and the null slot was overwritten. Feedback lines marked 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' are noted per instructions (not blocking), but the underlying mechanism (semantic rules clobbering planted NULLs) should be fixed so nullable columns that are rule targets (College, Draft_Pick_Number, Position) always preserve at least one planted NULL.
issues.requested_revision: Preserve NULL entries through _apply_semantic_rules (three-valued logic — already done for some, verify all rule paths) and always re-verify after shaping that every nullable column has ≥1 NULL row.

unresolved_checks: Could not verify per-instance NULL share vs compact share directly (aggregated feedback only).

Could not confirm that match_season → country/team parent rows are inserted before children in every instance except by reading table_order logic; the sibling FK violation ~411/20 instances suggests table order and PK-dedup interactions need a fix and re-run.
Semantic formula 'Season BETWEEN 1990 AND 2010' appears supported; the WL '%-%' rule is supported; Position IN-domain is supported but conflicts with the boundary-target pool (designer fix needed).

issues.evidence: The specification's per_column_exceptions list includes PK columns (country.Country_id, team.Team_id) with 'unmatched_join_rows' targets, and the atomic-operations extraction lists duplicates_for_distinct/group_sizes targets on country.Country_id (e.g. 'duplicate_share 20-50%', 'group_sizes 1,2,>=3'). The specification's own 'uncertainty' field and the generic int_primary_key rule correctly override these ('PK duplicate/group targets removed to preserve sequential uniqueness'). The program implements the override (DISTINCT_TARGETS/GROUP_TARGETS exclude PKs; _assign_primary_keys is sequential). This is internally consistent, but the spec text still carries contradictory PK targets that could mislead a future implementer.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the PK duplicate/group targets from per_column_exceptions (or explicitly annotate them as overridden by int_primary_key) so the spec is self-consistent. No program change needed.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows match_season generated rows are NULL 20/20 for every nullable column (College, Country, Draft_Class, Draft_Pick_Number, Player, Position, Team). This is because choose_table_sizes varies the target (16 * 0.5..1.5) and _apply_null_rule / fill_foreign_keys_consistently plant at least one NULL per nullable column; with small n the NULL share (>=5%, at least 1 row) can consume the whole column. The interface note says a 'NULL 0/n' line is non-blocking, but the inverse (all-NULL) is not addressed. It does not violate integrity (0 FK/NOT NULL/PK violations) and non-NULL values still exist in the compact rows, but generated-row value variation for match_season is effectively lost.
issues.requested_revision: In _apply_null_rule and fill_foreign_keys_consistently, cap the number of planted NULLs at n-1 (leave at least one non-NULL generated value per nullable column) so generated rows retain value variation. This is a robustness improvement, not a blocking error.

issues.evidence: The specification's text_boundary rule says 'include the exact literal and one lexicographic step on each side', but BOUNDARY for match_season.Position is restricted to the uppercase IN-domain ['Defender','Midfielder','Forward'] (designer's stated fix to align boundary with IN-domain). The program's _sample_column for BOUNDARY keys draws 70% from the domain and 30% perturbed pool values, then _apply_semantic_rules coerces any out-of-domain Position back into the enum. This is consistent with the designer's supporting_evidence note, but the generic text_boundary rule and the per-column exception are in tension; the program resolves it correctly.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the spec that for match_season.Position the boundary pool is the IN-domain enum (no lexicographic neighbours), matching the program. No program change needed.
